automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.rule: Only include sources published or visibly updated within the last seven days relative to run time.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: Article page/search result visible publication date within the cutoff window.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article argues that coding agents stall before production when organizations lack policy-as-code enforcement, identity boundaries, sandboxing, human approval gates, and monitoring for autonomous execution.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The selected lifecycle, harness, MCP/tool governance, and telemetry leaves can use this source as raw evidence that production agent workflows need explicit execution boundaries and observable control points, not only better prompts.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Keep future downstream synthesis focused on local gate placement, harness responsibilities, and telemetry requirements; broad product/entity background belongs upstream.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Consider ingesting into governance and harness leaves together rather than duplicating the same controls in each page.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: GitHub repository API reports updated_at 2026-07-19T20:18:26Z and pushed_at 2026-07-19T20:48:05Z.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The public Microsoft repository describes an AI Agent Governance Toolkit for policy enforcement, zero-trust identity, execution sandboxing, and reliability engineering for autonomous AI agents.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The repository is current public evidence that governance is being packaged as reusable harness infrastructure, which maps directly to local subagent coordination, agent harness, and tool-call governance practices.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Route broad toolkit/entity coverage upstream; locally, preserve the practice implication that agent harnesses should make identity, policy, sandbox, and reliability controls explicit components.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: During ingest, prefer the repository and API timestamps as provenance and avoid treating popularity metrics as adoption evidence.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: Post URL and page metadata indicate July 2026 publication, with search result showing July 15 inside the window.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The post reflects on coding-agent work as a ship-shape practice: stronger models make faster progress, but durable results still depend on prompts, decomposition, review, and testable delivery habits.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: This is practitioner evidence for keeping use/compose/build workflow selection and TDD guidance centered on controllable work shape rather than model choice alone.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Synthesize as a local workflow-shaping example, not as broad Claude Code product coverage.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Check whether the local AI-assisted TDD page needs a short note on tests as the stabilizer for agent-generated implementation bursts.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: Search result shows July 14, 2026 publication inside the window.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article summarizes 2026 AI agent adoption patterns, including agentic systems that plan, execute, use tools, maintain memory, and coordinate multiple specialized agents.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The local application-pattern leaves can use it as dated adoption context for why workflow state, runtime telemetry, and multi-agent coordination need first-class application surfaces.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: Search result and newsletter page indicate July 18, 2026 publication inside the window.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The newsletter reports on HalluSquatting, where LLMs can invent package names that attackers may later register, turning generated dependency suggestions into a supply-chain risk.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: This supports local guidance that request packages, retrieval evidence, RAG provenance, and tool-call governance must distinguish generated suggestions from verified repository or package-index facts.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Ingest as a concrete boundary for dependency/tool suggestions: require citation-backed package identity before install or code generation changes.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Use the newsletter only as a dated public pointer; verify technical details against the original paper or package-index evidence during synthesis.
